questions.q: State the definition of mean free path and write its exact formula in terms of molecular diameter \(d\) and number density \(n\). What is its SI unit?
questions.a: Mean free path (\(\lambda\)) is the average distance a molecule travels between two successive collisions. Exact formula: \(\lambda = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2} \pi d^2 n}\). SI unit: metre (m). A wrong answer (e.g., omitting \(\sqrt{2}\) or using \(r\) instead of \(d\)) reveals confusion between the simplified derivation (stationary targets) and the exact result (moving targets), or confusion between radius and diameter.

questions.q: In the exact derivation of mean free path, a factor of \(1/\sqrt{2}\) appears compared to the simplified derivation. Explain physically why this factor arises and what assumption about the other molecules is relaxed.
questions.a: The simplified derivation assumes all other molecules are at rest. In reality, all molecules move with a distribution of velocities. The collision rate depends on the average relative speed \(\langle v_r \rangle\), not the average speed \(\langle v \rangle\). For a Maxwellian distribution, \(\langle v_r \rangle = \sqrt{2} \langle v \rangle\). Since collision frequency is proportional to relative speed, the mean free path decreases by \(1/\sqrt{2}\). A wrong answer indicates the student has memorised the formula without understanding the role of relative motion in collision kinetics.

questions.q: Calculate the mean free path of nitrogen molecules at STP (0°C, 1 atm). Given: molecular diameter of N₂ = 3.7 Å, molar volume at STP = 22.4 L. Show all steps with units.
questions.a:
Step 1: Number density \(n = \frac{N_A}{V_m} = \frac{6.022 \times 10^{23}}{22.4 \times 10^{-3}} = 2.69 \times 10^{25} \text{ m}^{-3}\).
Step 2: Diameter \(d = 3.7 \text{ Å} = 3.7 \times 10^{-10} \text{ m}\).
Step 3: \(\lambda = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2} \pi d^2 n} = \frac{1}{1.414 \times 3.14 \times (3.7 \times 10^{-10})^2 \times 2.69 \times 10^{25}}\).
Step 4: \(d^2 = 13.69 \times 10^{-20} \text{ m}^2\); denominator \(= 1.414 \times 3.14 \times 13.69 \times 10^{-20} \times 2.69 \times 10^{25} \approx 1.63 \times 10^7 \text{ m}^{-1}\).
Step 5: \(\lambda \approx 6.1 \times 10^{-8} \text{ m} = 61 \text{ nm}\).
A wrong answer (e.g., 43 nm) suggests the student forgot the \(\sqrt{2}\) factor or used radius instead of diameter. Unit mismatch (e.g., cm) reveals carelessness in converting Å to m.

questions.q: A gas is kept at constant temperature. If its pressure is doubled, how does the mean free path change? Justify using the formula and the ideal gas law.
questions.a: From ideal gas law, \(P = n k_B T\). At constant \(T\), \(n \propto P\). Since \(\lambda \propto 1/n\), doubling \(P\) doubles \(n\), so \(\lambda\) halves. A wrong answer (e.g., \(\lambda\) unchanged or doubled) shows the student does not connect number density to pressure via the ideal gas law, or thinks molecular diameter changes with pressure.

questions.q: A student derives \(\lambda = \frac{1}{\pi d^2 n}\) by assuming a moving molecule collides with stationary molecules. They claim this is correct because "on average, the other molecules are at rest". Evaluate this claim and identify the error.
questions.a: The claim is incorrect. Even though the average velocity of all molecules is zero, the average relative speed between two molecules is not zero. For a Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution, the average relative speed is \(\sqrt{2}\) times the average speed. Ignoring the motion of target molecules underestimates the collision frequency by \(\sqrt{2}\) and overestimates \(\lambda\) by \(\sqrt{2}\). The error is confusing the average velocity (vector, zero) with the average relative speed (scalar, non-zero).

questions.q: Design a thought experiment to estimate the diameter of an air molecule using only macroscopic measurements of mean free path (e.g., by measuring viscosity or diffusion). Outline the steps and the formula you would use.
questions.a: (1) Measure the viscosity of air at a known temperature and pressure, (2) Use the kinetic-theory relation eta equals one-third n m v-bar lambda to obtain the mean free path from the measured viscosity, (3) Calculate n as P over k T, m as M over N A, and v-bar as the square root of eight k T over pi m, (4) Solve lambda equals one over root-two pi d squared n for the molecular diameter d. A poor answer omits the connection between viscosity and mean free path, or fails to identify all the measurable quantities needed.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Mean free path is the average distance traveled by a gas molecule between two ______ collisions with other molecules.
Fill in the blank: Observe that when a gas cylinder leaks in a kitchen, the smell takes minutes to reach the other corner even though ______ move at ~500 m/s.
What is Mean free path? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Mean free path is the average distance traveled by a gas molecule between two successive collisions with other molecules.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Observe that when a gas cylinder leaks in a kitchen, the smell takes minutes to reach the other corner even though molecules move at ~______ m/s.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student can derive the mean free path formula from collision geometry, calculate it for a given gas using number density and molecular diameter, and explain why it is much larger than the intermolecular distance in gases.
